english: There is a great remove between Christians and the people of this present world. Those who have the spirit of the world are bound, heart and mind, in earthly fetters; but those who long for the love of the heavenly Father keep him alone before their eyes with a single desire.

The Christian's world is another world: another way of life, another mind, another speech, another deed. The world's people have their own way, mind, speech, and deed. The two are not the same kind of thing. When love of the world weighs even a little in the heart's yoke, the evil logos at once comes forward as far as the lips, and the mind stretches darts from within and wounds the neighbor through the tongue — seeking its own glory of its own will.

From this root every evil grows: theft, gluttony, lust, vainglory, anger, love of money, love of honor — every passion. God says, 'I am a jealous God' (Exodus 20:5). He scatters the bones of those who please themselves (Psalm 53:6). Whoever loves anything of the world binds himself under the yoke of his own will. The Christian must not be a man-pleaser (Galatians 1:10); 'friendship with the world is enmity with God' (James 4:4).

The Lord shows that those who follow the deceits and wills of the evil one bear Cain's image of wickedness: 'You wish to do the desires of your father; he was a murderer from the beginning, and does not stand in the truth' (John 8:44). So the whole sinful race of Adam holds that sentence in secret — trembling and shaken in the sieve of the earth by the sieving Satan. As from one Adam the race was spread over the earth, so one wickedness of the passions has sunk into the sinful race, and the ruler of wickedness tosses all in restless, material, empty, troubled thoughts.

As one wind can shake every plant and seed, or one night's darkness cover the whole inhabited world, so the ruler of wickedness — a rational darkness of evil and death, a hidden fierce wind — tosses every race of people on earth, carrying them about in restless thoughts and worldly desires, filling every soul not born from above with darkness of ignorance, dullness, and forgetfulness.

True Christians differ from the whole race of people here: their mind and understanding remain in a heavenly way of thinking, and they behold the eternal goods by sharing in the Holy Spirit. They flee the world's desire and seek the heavenly treasure; they renounce self and the world and cleave to the Father alone. 'Where your treasure is, there your heart will be also' (Matthew 6:21). Do not love the world or the things in the world (1 John 2:15-17).

english: Let us then struggle by faith and a virtuous way of life to gain that garment here and now, so that when we put on the body we may not be found naked, with nothing to glorify our flesh on that day. Each person is counted worthy, by faith and zeal, to share as much of the Spirit as he can hold; that measure becomes the covering of immortality.

Those who are Christians in truth and power take courage and rejoice when they leave the flesh, because they already have that house not made with hands — the power of the Spirit dwelling in them. If the house of the body is taken down, they do not fear: they have the heavenly house of the Spirit and that incorruptible glory which, on the day of resurrection, will also build and glorify the house of the body. As the Apostle says: 'He who raised Christ from the dead will also give life to your mortal bodies through his Spirit who dwells in you' (Romans 8:11). And again: that the life of Jesus may be shown in our mortal flesh, and that what is mortal may be swallowed up by life (2 Corinthians 5:4).

All these things are examples, types, and images of Christians in the resurrection. For every God-loving soul — that is, for true Christians — there is first a Xanthicus, called April, which is the day of the resurrection. By the power of the sun of righteousness (Malachi 4:2) the glory of the Holy Spirit comes out from within, covering and sheltering the bodies of the saints — the same glory they already held hidden in their souls. What the soul has now comes then outside the body. This first month brings joy to all creation: it clothes bare trees, opens the earth, gives gladness to every living thing. So for Christians Xanthicus is the season of the resurrection, when their bodies will be glorified by the ineffable light already in them — the power of the Spirit, which will then be for them garment, food, drink, exultation, joy, peace, clothing, and eternal life.

Question: Can Satan be united with God? Answer: The sun, though a creature, shines on filth and is not defiled; how much more the divine and heavenly fire, when it meets the devil, is not defiled but burns away what is evil. God allowed evil as a gymnasium for human beings — for testing and training. Therefore each of us must believe, endure, and press on in every virtuous practice, so as to be found worthy of the heavenly garment and the glory of the Holy Spirit in the inner person, that our bodies also may be raised and live. 'This mortal must put on immortality' (1 Corinthians 15:53).
